messages.author: e29bb582075d5997
messages.subject: Aerial counting with UAV in 'distance'
parts:
Dear All,

I have aerial counting data of pinnipeds. We were shooting the water area from a long-range unmanned aircraft. As a result, we have a continuous transect of images.

All images were studied, and the number of individuals in each image, where they were, was counted. It is necessary to calculate the abundance of marine mammls and build a map with environmental covariates (ice conditions, depth, etc).

I just can't figure out how to use distance to solve this problem. After all, we do not have a detection function in this case?

Probably a similar question has been discussed before, but I couldn't find it. I will be very grateful for your advice!

Sincerely

Sergey

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] Aerial counting with UAV in 'distance'
parts:
Sergey

Depending upon how the images were taken (for example, looking vertically to the water) so that detectability is perfect from the centre to the edge of the images, then it is not a distance sampling problem.  Distance sampling is used to determine the probability of detection given that detectability is perfect on the flight line and diminishes with distance from the flight line.

Instead, you have what is called a "strip transect" where all animals within the strip are detected.  However an added complication is whether you are counting detections only of animals on the surface or are animals under the surface being detected.  That raises issues of availability to be detected.

You may want to consult the following papers:

Stevenson, BC, Borchers, DL, Fewster, RM. Cluster capture-recapture to account for identification uncertainty on aerial surveys of animal populations. Biometrics. 2018; 1– 11. https://doi.org/10.1111/biom.12983 

Buckland, S.T., Burt, M.L., Rexstad, E.A., Mellor, M., Williams, A.E. and Woodward, R. (2012), Aerial surveys of seabirds: the advent of digital methods. Journal of Applied Ecology, 49: 960-967. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2664.2012.02150.x  [this deals with seabirds and strip transect analysis, does not address animal availability]

Hello Sergey,
 
 
I think that density surface modelling can be used in this case (dsm package). It has an option for using strip transects (no need for detection function), and each image would turn into transect segment in this case.
 
 
Best wishes,
 
Mikhail
